text:
jamie: Heads up — after last night's deploy we saw a spike in cross-region LB ejections and downstream TLS handshake retries. Postmortem linked but we need a concise action tracker here. :rotating_light:
lei: saw the same. LB logs show healthcheck flaps leading to backend ejects in us-east-1 -> eu-west-1 paths. TLS failed on ~0.4% of connections during spikes.
maria: adding notes from the PM: traffic surge + slightly higher RTTs triggered our fail-fast policy. Looks like the routing bug amplified retries across regions.
sujay: quick triage summary I pushed to the postmortem: load-balancer config had an aggressive outlier detection rule + outdated certs on a subset of backends, but the certs were not the dominant failure cause. Root cause leans routing/healthcheck timing.
jamie: action items proposal: 1) revert aggressive outlier threshold to previous baseline (owner: lei, due: 2026-04-05) 2) add short-term TLS alert for cert handshake error rates (owner: sujay, due: 2026-03-30) 3) runbook update for cross-region retries and failover (owner: maria, due: 2026-04-09) 4) long-term: implement coordinated drain + cooldown before ejects (owner: eng-runtime team, ticket INF-2523, due: 2026-05-15).
lei: I can take #1. I'll open a small change and can do a canary tomorrow morning. Will annotate rollback window.
maria: taking #3 — will create PR on docs and add a short checklist for oncall to follow during region flaps.
sujay: created INF-2523 for the coordinated drain plan. I'll add a design sketch by EOD and sync with runtime folks. Also enabling a temporary Prometheus alert for TLS handshake rate > 0.2% over 5m.
jamie: devbot: can you add a reminder card in the incidents board for these due dates?
devbot: reminder created: INF-2523 (long-term), CHG-1874 (outlier revert), DOC-998 (runbook).
lei: quick status check — CHG-1874 draft created, tag @eng-oncall for canary at 06:00 UTC.
maria: DOC-998 PR created and referencing the postmortem. Will add runbook playbook steps and links to the new alert.
sujay: note about recurrence: history shows a small cluster of similar incidents over the past 9 months spaced ~6-8 weeks apart when traffic patterns spike. We should consider automated smoothing rather than manual thresholds. Adding to INF-2523 scope.
jamie: agreed, make smoothing/gradual-eject part of the design. Also we need an ownership matrix for cross-region routing: who owns which policy — suggest netops + runtime collab.
lei: pinging @sujay and @jamie for a short 30-min sync tomorrow to walk through the canary plan.
sujay: ack. I'll include perf graphs and a short replay of the LB logs.
jamie: final notes for this thread: owners and dates locked in; I'll run a weekly check-in until INF-2523 is closed. If anyone notices repeat ejects in the meantime, tag this thread. :eyes:
maria: thanks — will post runbook link once PR merges.
lei: oncall will monitor the canary window and report back in this thread.
jamie: closing the thread for now, will reopen if new failures surface.
